note: PLACEHOLDER. Every params object here validates against the published self_research manifest input_schema (additionalProperties: false, $refs inlined the way publish_experiments.py inlines them), and every value is plausible, but nobody has dispatched one. So a verdict drawn from this list is a claim about the pipeline, not about the agent. EIGHT cases, and DEFAULT_JUDGE_CONFIG.gates.minCases is 20. A corpus verdict over this list therefore resolves CAN'T SAY however the judge voted, because the floor was set from measured agent non-determinism and eight runs measure that rather than the branch. Eight is deliberate and not a rounding error: one clean baseline plus seven single-axis variations is what one change can author honestly across nine agents. Whether to grow every list to 20 or to lower the floor is still open — do not read the shortfall as a decision. Varied along: hint richness, from a case carrying website, socials, coverage URLs and prior roles down to one carrying only the three required fields — this is the agent that has to find its own subject, so how much of the footprint is handed to it is the main axis; whether the candidate has a public record to research (multi-term incumbent with prior roles) or none at all (first-time candidate, empty prior_roles); city supplied, explicitly null, or omitted, which is what separates a same-named person in another jurisdiction; and a large city where news coverage is dense against a rural county and a small borough where there may be one weekly paper and no archive. People are fictional placeholders in the house style (gp-webapp e2e-tests briefings.spec.ts uses 'Test Official'); this file is public, so no real person is named. States, cities, office titles and L2 voter file column names are real.
